questions.q: Two open organ pipes of lengths $60 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $90 \mathrm{~cm}$ resonate at $6^{\text {th }}$ and $5^{\text {th }}$ harmonics respectively. The difference of frequencies for the given modes is _______ $\mathrm{Hz}$. (Velocity of sound in air $=333 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: The equation of wave is given by& $Y = {10}^{- 2}sin2\pi \left($160t - 0 . 5x + $\dfrac{π}{4}\right), where $x$ and $Y$ are in $m$ and $t$ in $s$. The speed of the wave is _______~$kmh^{- 1}$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The equation of the wave is&

$Y = {10}^{- 2}sin2\pi ( 160t - 0 . 5x + \dfrac{π}{4} )$

The velocity of a wave is given by~$v = \dfrac{ω}{k} . . . ( i )$.

A wave equation is given by~

$Y = Asin \left(\omegat -kx + ϕ\right)$

Using equation (i),

$v = \left(\dfrac{2\pi \times 160}{2\pi \times 0 .5}\right) =320ms^{- 1}$

$⇒ v = 320 \times \dfrac{18}{5}$

$⇒ v = 1152kmh^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: Two travelling waves of equal amplitudes and equal frequencies move in opposite directions along a string. They interfere to produce a stationary wave whose equation is given by& $y = \left(10cos\pixsin\dfrac{2\pit}{T}\right)cm$. The amplitude of the particle at $x = \dfrac{4}{3}cm$ will be _____~$cm .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position, for that

$sin\left(\dfrac{2\pit}{T}\right) = 1$

Therefore,~$A = \left|10cos\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\right)\right| = 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 5cm$

questions.q: Two waves are simultaneously passing through a string and their equations are : ${y}_{1} = {A}_{1}sink ( x - vt ) , {y}_{2} = {A}_{2}sink\left(x - vt + {x}_{0}\right) .$ Given amplitudes ${A}_{1} = 12mm$ and ${A}_{2} = 5mm$,~ ${x}_{0} = 3 . 5cm$ and wave number $k = 6 . 28{cm}^{- 1} .$ The amplitude of resulting wave will be _____~$mm .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\Deltaϕ = {kx}_{0} = \dfrac{2\pi}{λ}{x}_{0} = 2\pi \times 3 . 5 \left(\lambda = $\dfrac{2\pi}{k} =$1\right)$

$= 2\pi \times $\dfrac{35}{10} ==$7\pi

${A}_{R} = \sqrt{{12}^{2} + {5}^{2} + 2 \times 12 \times 5 \times cos ( 7\pi )} = \sqrt{( 12 - 5{)}^{2}} =7$ mm

$

questions.q: A tuning fork resonates with a sonometer wire of length $1m$ stretched with a tension of $6N .$ When the tension in the wire is changed to $54N,$ the same tuning fork produces $12$ beats per second with it. The frequency of the tuning fork is _______ $Hz .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Frequency of sonometer wire is given by, $f = \dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}}$

Therefore, ${f}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{6}{μ}}{f}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{54}{μ}}$

Hence, $\dfrac{f1}{f2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Also it is given that, ${f}_{2} - {f}_{1} = 12$

So, ${f}_{1} = 6Hz$.

questions.q: The fundamental frequency of vibration of a string between two rigid support is $50$ Hz. The mass of the string is $18g$ and its linear mass density is $20gm^{- 1}$. The speed of the transverse waves so produced in the string is _______ $ms^{– 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The fundamental frequency is& $f = 50Hz$.

The length of the~string is~$l = \dfrac{λ}{2}$

Linear mass density is~$\mu = \dfrac{m}{l} = 20gm^{- 1}$

Using~$v = f\lambda$

$\dfrac{v}{2l} = 50$

$⇒ v = 100 \times l = \dfrac{100 \times 18}{20} = 90ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two travelling waves produces a standing wave represented by equation. $y = \left(1 . 0mm\right)cos \left[  \left($1 . 57{cm}^{- 1}\right)x\right]sin\left[\left(78 . 5s^{- 1}\right)t\right]$. The node closest to the origin in the region $x > 0$~will be at $x = . . . . . . \left(\text{in}cm\right) .$
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of $20 . 0cm$ for a tuning fork of frequency $400$ Hz is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is $336\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of _____~$cm$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Wavelength of wave $⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{336}{400} = 84cm$

At first resonance

$\dfrac{λ}{4} = l + e ⇒ \dfrac{84}{4} = 20 + e$, where,~$e$~is end correction.

$⇒ e = 1$
So third resonance length

$5\dfrac{λ}{4} = {l}_{2} + e$

$5\left(21\right) = {l}_{2} + 1$

${l}_{2} = 104cm$

questions.q: The distance between two consecutive points with phase difference of $60 °$ in a wave of frequency $500$ Hz is $6 . 0m$. The velocity with which wave is travelling is ______~$kms^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Distance between two consecutive points& $60 °$~out of phase is given by~$\Deltax = \dfrac{λ}{2\pi}\Deltaϕ$

Putting the values, we have

$6 = \dfrac{λ}{2\pi} \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)

$⇒ \lambda = 36m$

Now, velocity of wave is~$v = f\lambda = ( 500Hz ) ( 36m )$

$= 18000ms^{- 1} = 18kms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: A wire having a linear mass density $9 . 0 \times {10}^{- 4}kgm^{- 1}$ is stretched between two rigid supports with a tension of $900N .$~The wire resonates at a frequency of $500Hz .$~The next higher frequency at which the same wire resonates is $550Hz .$~The length of the wire is ___________~$m .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${f}_{n} = \dfrac{nv}{2ℓ} = 500$
${f}_{n + 1} = \dfrac{( n + 1 ) v}{2ℓ} = 550$
$\dfrac{n + 1}{n} = \dfrac{11}{10}$
Thus, $n = 10$
Thus,~$ℓ = \dfrac{nv}{2{f}_{n}} \left($v = $\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}}\right)
$= $\dfrac{10}{2 \times 500} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{900}{9 \times {10}^{- 4}}} =$10m

questions.q: The amplitude of wave disturbance propagating in the positive $x$-direction is given by $y = \dfrac{1}{( 1 + x{)}^{2}}$ at time $t = 0$~and $y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - 2{)}^{2}}$ at $t = 1s$, where $x$~and $y$ are in metres. The shape of wave does not change during the propagation. The velocity of the wave will be $ms^{- 1} .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At $t = 0, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}$
At time $t = t, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - vt{)}^{2}}$
At $t = 1, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - v{)}^{2}} \ldots ( i )$
At $t = 1, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - 2{)}^{2}} \ldots ( ii )$
Comparing $( i ) and ( ii )$
$v = 2ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A closed and an open organ pipe have same lengths. If the ratio of frequencies of their seventh overtones is  \left(\frac{a-1}{a}\right)$ then the value of $\mathrm{a}$ is ________$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For closed organ pipe
$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}=(2 \mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell}=\frac{15 \mathrm{v}}{4 \ell}$
For open organ pipe
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}=(\mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \ell}=\frac{8 \mathrm{v}}{2 \ell} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}}=\frac{15}{16}=\frac{\mathrm{a}-1}{\mathrm{a}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=16\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A wire of length $30$ cm, stretched between rigid supports, has it's $n^{th}$ and \left(n + 1\right)th$~harmonics at $400$ Hz and $450$ Hz, respectively. If tension in the string is $2700N$, it's linear mass density is _____ $kgm^{- 1}$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Frequency of& $n^{th}$~harmonic is~$\dfrac{nv}{2l} = 400 ⇒ \dfrac{nv}{0 . 6} = 400 . . . \left(1\right)$~

And frequency of~\left(n + 1\right)th$~harmonic is~\dfrac{ \left(n + 1\right)v}{2l} =$450 ⇒ \dfrac{ \left(n + 1\right)v}${0 . 6} =$450 . . . \left(2\right)$, here,~$v$~is speed of wave on string.~

From equation~ \left(1\right)$, we have

$n = \dfrac{400 \times 0 . 6}{v}$

Putting in equation~ \left(2\right)$,~

$⇒ \$left[\dfrac{0 . 6 \times 400}{v} +$1\right]\dfrac{v}{0 . 6} =450$

$⇒ \left[400 + \dfrac{v}{0 . 6}\right] =450$

$⇒ v = 30ms^{- 1}$

Speed of wave on string is stated as~$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}} =30$, here,~$\mu$~is linear mass density.

So,~$\mu = \dfrac{T}{v2} = \dfrac{2700}{900}⇒ \mu = 3kgm^{- 1}$

questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave passing through a string of length $50$ cm and mass $10g$ is $60ms^{- 1}$. The area of cross-section of the wire is $2 . 0{mm}^{2}$ and its Young's modulus is $1 . 2 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$. The extension of the wire over its natural length due to its tension will be $x \times {10}^{- 5}m$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The wave speed in string is given by& ${v}_{w} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}}$, where,~$T$~is tension and~$\mu = \dfrac{m}{l}$~is linear mass density.

Putting the values, we have

$⇒ 60 = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{10 \times {10}^{- 3}} \times 0 . 5}$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{\left(60\right)2 \times {10}^{- 2}}{0 . 5} = 72N$

The Young's modulus is given by~$Y = \dfrac{Fl}{A ∆ l}$, here,~$A$~is area.

From above the extension of the wire~is~$\Deltal = \dfrac{Tl}{AY} = \dfrac{72 \times 0 . 5}{2 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 1 . 2 \times {10}^{11}}= \dfrac{72 \times 5}{24} \times {10}^{- 5} = 15 \times {10}^{- 5}m$.

Hence, the value of~$x = 15$.

questions.q: A guitar string of length $90$ cm vibrates with a fundamental frequency of $120$ Hz. The length of the string producing a fundamental of $180$ Hz will be _____~$cm$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency produced in a vibrating string is given by

${f}_{0} = \dfrac{v}{2L} . . . \left(1\right)$

For the first case, it can be written that

$120 = $\dfrac{v}{2 ( 90 )} . . . \left(2\right)$

Similarly, for the second case, it can be written that

$180 = $\dfrac{v}{2 ( L )} . . . \left(3\right)$

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) and solve to obtain the required length of the string.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{180}{120}& = & \dfrac{\dfrac{v}{2\left(L\right)}}{\dfrac{v}{2\left(90\right)}}\\ & = & \dfrac{90}{L}\\ & ⇒ & L = 90 $\times $\dfrac{120}{180}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 60\end{cases}$ \text{ and }

$

questions.q: In a closed organ pipe, the frequency of fundamental note is $30$ Hz. A certain amount of water is now poured in the organ pipe so that the fundamental frequency is increased to $110$ Hz. If the organ pipe has a cross-sectional area of $2{cm}^{2}$, the amount of water poured in the organ tube is ________g$. (Take speed of sound in air is $330ms^{- 1} )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fundamental frequency for closed organ pipe in the first part:

$\dfrac{V}{4{l}_{1}} = 30 ⇒ {l}_{1} = \dfrac{11}{4}m$

Similarly, for second part:

$\dfrac{V}{4{l}_{2}} = 110 ⇒ {l}_{2} = \dfrac{3}{4}m$

Therefore, change in length $\Deltal = 2m$

Change in volume $= A \Deltal = 400{cm}^{3}$

$M = 400g; \left(∵ ρ = 1g{cm}^{- 3}\right)

$

questions.q: For a certain organ pipe, the first three resonance frequencies are in the ratio of $1: 3: 5$ respectively. If the frequency of fifth harmonic is $405$ Hz and the speed of sound in air is $324ms^{– 1}$ the length of the organ pipe is _____ $m$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given,

${f}_{5} = 405Hz$.

As the first three resonance frequencies are in the ratio of~$1: 3: 5$, therefore it must be a closed organ pipe.

The frequency formula in a closed organ pipe is given by~$f = \dfrac{nv}{4l}$. So,

$\dfrac{5v}{4I} = 405Hz$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{405 \times 4}{5 \times 324} = 1m$

questions.q: In an experiment with sonometer when a mass of $180g$ is attached to the string, it vibrates with fundamental frequency of $30$ Hz. When a mass~$m$ is attached, the string vibrates with fundamental frequency of $50$ Hz. The value of $m$ is ______ $g$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency in a stretched string is given by

$f = \dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}} . . . \left(1\right)$

For the first mass, it can be written that

${f}_{1} = $\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{1}g}{μ}} . . . \left(2\right)$

And, for the second mass, it can be written that

${f}_{2} = $\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{2}g}{μ}} . . . \left(3\right)$

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required mass.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{f2}{f1}& = & \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{2}g}{μ}}}{\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{1}g}{μ}}}\\ & = & \sqrt{\dfrac{m2}{m1}}\\ & ⇒ & \dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = $\$left(\dfrac{f1}{f2}\right)2 \\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } {m}_{2} = {m}_{1}\$left(\dfrac{{f}_{2}}{{f}_{1}}\right)$2 . . . \left(4\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (4) to calculate the required mass.

\begin{cases}{m}_{2}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 180g \times \left(\dfrac{50Hz}{30Hz}\right)$2 \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 500g\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A tuning fork is vibrating at $250$ Hz. The length of the shortest closed organ pipe that will resonate with the tuning fork will be _____cm$. (Take speed of sound in air as $340\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1} )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For closed organ pipe

$f = ( 2n + 1 ) \dfrac{v}{4l}$

for minimum length, $n = 0$

${f}_{0} = \dfrac{v}{4l}$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{v}{4{f}_{0}}$

$= \dfrac{340}{4 \times 250} = 34cm$

questions.q: A wire of density $8 \times {10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$~is stretched between two clamps $0 . 5m$ apart. The extension developed in the wire is $3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 4}m$. If $Y = 8 \times {10}^{10}Nm^{- 2}$, the fundamental frequency of vibration in the wire will be _____~$Hz$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using the relation of Young's modulus,

& $\dfrac{T}{A} = Y \left(\dfrac{\Delta L}{L}\right)$
$⇒ T = $\$left(\dfrac{Y\Delta L}{L} \timesA\right)

The linear mass density is~$\mu = \$left(\dfrac{m}{L}\right).$

So,
$\dfrac{T}{μ} = \dfrac{Y\Delta LA}{L\left(\dfrac{m}{L}\right)} = \dfrac{Y ( \Delta L ) \times LA}{L ( m )} =\$left(\dfrac{Y\Delta L}{L}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{1}{ρ}\right)

Substituting the values,
\dfrac{T}{μ} = \dfrac{8 \times {10}^{10} \times 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 4}}{0 . 5} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{8 \times {10}^{3}}\right) =$6 . 4 \times {10}^{3}$
$⇒ $\dfrac{T}{μ} =$64 \times {10}^{2}$

The fundamental frequency is given by~$f = $\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}}.
$⇒ $\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}} =$8 \times10 = 80ms^{- 1}$
Therefore,

$f = \left(\dfrac{80}{1}\right) =80$ Hz

$
